# statuspal-next_container (Resource)

Manages a container (service group / region) on a StatusPal Next status page. Service membership is managed automatically: every existing service is assigned to a new container (full N×M grid).

~> **Note:** Every status page is created with a `Default` container automatically. To manage that container with Terraform, import it (`terraform import ... <subdomain>/default`) rather than declaring a new one with the same name, which would create a second container.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "statuspal-next_status_page" "acme" {
  name        = "Acme Status"
  subdomain   = "acme-status"
  timezone    = "America/New_York"
  website_url = "https://acme.com"
}

resource "statuspal-next_container" "eu" {
  status_page_subdomain = statuspal-next_status_page.acme.subdomain
  name                  = "EU Region"
}

# Every status page is created with a "Default" container automatically. Import
# it instead of declaring a second container with the same name:
#   terraform import statuspal-next_container.default acme-status/default
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the container (e.g. `EU Region`).
- `status_page_subdomain` (String) Subdomain of the status page the container belongs to. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `slug` (String) URL-safe identifier, unique per status page. If omitted it is auto-generated from `name` (collisions get a numeric suffix).

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp at which the container was created.
- `id` (String) Server-generated identifier of the container.
- `services` (Attributes List) Services assigned to this container, with their live status (read-only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--services))
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp at which the container was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--services"></a>
### Nested Schema for `services`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) Service name.
- `slug` (String) Service slug.
- `status` (String) Live status of the service in this container.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Containers are imported as "<status_page_subdomain>/<container_slug>".
terraform import statuspal-next_container.eu acme-status/eu-region
```
